# Psalm 102 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A-prayer of-the-afflicted when-he-faints and-before YHWH pours-out his-complaint.

**2** O-YHWH hear my-prayer, and-let-my-cry come to-you.

**3** Do-not hide your-face from-me in-day-of my-distress; incline to-me your-ear; in-day I-call answer-me quickly.

**4** For have-vanished like-smoke my-days, and-my-bones like-a-hearth burn.

**5** Is-struck like-grass and-withered my-heart, for I-forget to-eat my-bread.

**6** From-voice-of my-groaning has-clung my-bone to-my-flesh.

**7** I-am-like a-pelican-of the-wilderness; I-have-become like-an-owl-of ruins.

**8** I-lie-awake, and-I-am like-a-bird alone on a-roof.

**9** All the-day have-reproached-me my-enemies; those-mocking-me by-me they-swear.

**10** For ashes like-bread I-eat, and-my-drink with-weeping I-mingle,

**11** Because-of your-indignation and-your-wrath, for you-have-lifted-me-up and-you-have-cast-me-away.

**12** My-days like-a-shadow lengthened, and-I like-grass wither.

**13** And-you O-YHWH to-forever sit, and-your-remembrance to-generation and-generation.

**14** You will-arise, you-will-have-compassion-on Zion, for it-is-time to-be-gracious-to-her, for has-come the-appointed-time.

**15** For have-delighted your-servants in-her-stones, and-her-dust they-cherish.

**16** And-will-fear the-nations the-name-of YHWH, and-all the-kings-of the-earth your-glory.

**17** For has-built YHWH Zion; he-has-appeared in-his-glory.

**18** He-has-turned to-the-prayer-of the-destitute, and-not he-has-despised their-prayer.

**19** Let-this-be-written for-a-generation to-come, and-a-people yet-to-be-created will-praise Yah.

**20** For he-has-looked-down from-height-of his-holiness; YHWH from-heaven to-earth has-looked,

**21** To-hear the-groaning-of the-prisoner, to-set-free the-children-of death,

**22** To-declare in-Zion the-name-of YHWH, and-his-praise in-Jerusalem,

**23** When-gather-together peoples together, and-kingdoms to-serve YHWH.

**24** He-has-humbled on-the-way my-strength; he-has-shortened my-days.

**25** I-say, 'My-God do-not take-me-away in-half my-days; through-generation-of generations your-years.'

**26** To-before the-earth you-founded, and-work-of your-hands the-heavens.

**27** They will-perish and-you will-stand; and-all-of-them like-a-garment will-wear-out; like-clothing you-will-change-them and-they-will-pass-away.

**28** And-you the-same, and-your-years not will-end.

**29** The-children-of your-servants will-dwell, and-their-seed before-you will-be-established.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **102:26-28**: Quoted in Hebrews 1:10-12 as applied to Christ. The contrast between creation's impermanence and God's unchanging nature is the psalm's theological climax.

- **102:19**: 'A-people yet-to-be-created' (am nivra') — the psalm is written for the future; its hope transcends the psalmist's own lifetime.

— EMET
